name: Earnings long straddle
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Underpriced Earnings Moves
caseLead: Buying a straddle before an earnings announcement can be profitable when the stock moves more than the option market had priced in. The pattern persists because option prices rely on the typical past reaction, while changes in guidance, trade policy and regulation can move individual stocks far more than that average.
caseRest: The main risk is paying option premiums for earnings announcements that produce smaller price moves than expected. Most straddles expire with a small loss, so the return depends on a few large winners and can be negative for several quarters in a row. Rehyn estimates that results are weakest when implied volatility is already high across the market, because straddles then cost more and the stock must move further to cover the premium.
figNote: Each card shows the share price move on the first trading day after results. Options on large US companies usually price a move of about 4% to 8% on results day, so the straddle gains when the actual move is larger and loses when it is smaller.

events.title: Netflix subscriber growth lifts the shares
events.text: Netflix reported fourth-quarter subscriber growth well above expectations in January 2013, and the shares rose about 42% the next day. The straddle gained because the move was far larger than the move options had priced.

events.title: Meta guidance cut removes a quarter of value
events.text: Meta Platforms warned of weaker revenue in February 2022 and cited Apple's privacy changes, and the shares fell about 26% in a day. The straddle gained because the fall was far larger than the move implied by option prices.

events.title: Russia exit contributes to Netflix subscriber loss
events.text: Netflix reported its first subscriber loss in a decade in April 2022, a result it linked partly to suspending service in Russia, and the shares fell about 35%. The straddle gained because the decline was much larger than the move options had priced.

events.title: Apple shares barely move after results
events.text: Apple reported a small fall in quarterly revenue in November 2023, and the shares closed about 0.5% lower the next day. The straddle lost because the move was far smaller than the 3% to 4% that options typically price for Apple.

events.title: UnitedHealth guidance cut follows higher medical costs
events.text: UnitedHealth cut its 2025 profit forecast in April 2025 after higher medical costs in its Medicare Advantage business, and the shares fell about 22% in a day. The straddle gained because the move was several times the size options had priced.

events.title: Nvidia shares barely move after results
events.text: Nvidia reported record revenue in August 2025 and excluded sales to China from its forecast because of US export licensing, yet the shares closed about 1% lower. The straddle lost because the move was much smaller than the move options had priced.

instrument: Single-stock options on US large-cap stocks; at-the-money straddles expiring within a week of results
rules: Straddles bought one to three days before results when the implied move is below the stock's average earnings move over the past eight quarters; closed after the announcement; exposure capped per stock
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads and commissions deducted on entry and exit
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from underpriced earnings moves to limited premium loss

legs.purpose: Gains when the stock rises by more than the premium paid
Gains when the stock falls by more than the premium paid
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: Implied move at least 20% below the stock's average earnings move over eight quarters
size: Premium capped at 0.25% of capital per stock and 6% in total
exit: Position closed at the next market open after results
stop: No price stop; loss limited to the premium paid
marketWatch: The size of implied earnings moves compared with the average reaction over recent quarters is the main indicator for this strategy. Trade policy statements, changes in company guidance and the busiest weeks of the reporting season matter because they change both the price of options and the size of the moves. Rehyn also watches how many companies have options pricing a smaller move than their past eight quarters delivered.

favourable.heading: Guidance changes surprise investors
favourable.text: Large guidance changes favour the strategy because they produce moves well beyond those implied by option prices. Netflix in January 2013 rose about 42% after results, several times the move options had priced.

favourable.heading: Policy shifts reach company earnings
favourable.text: Policy changes favour the strategy when they alter a company's revenue outlook without warning, because option prices rely on past reactions. UnitedHealth in April 2025 fell about 22% after a profit forecast cut linked to rising medical costs, which is several times a typical reaction.

favourable.heading: Low option prices before results
favourable.text: Low option prices before results favour the strategy because the premium paid is small compared with the moves that can follow. Nvidia in May 2023 rose about 24% after raising its forecast for chip demand, far above the move options had priced.

adverse.heading: Expensive options before results
adverse.text: High option prices before results hurt the strategy because the stock must move further than usual to cover the premium. Nvidia in August 2025 closed about 1% lower after results, well short of the move options had priced.

adverse.heading: Stable results with small reactions
adverse.text: Predictable results hurt the strategy because stocks with steady earnings rarely move by more than the options imply. Apple in November 2023 closed about 0.5% lower after results, so the premium paid decayed with little offsetting gain.

adverse.heading: Market-wide stress lifts premiums
adverse.text: Market-wide stress hurts the strategy when it lifts option prices for every stock at once, so straddles cost more even where results are routine. In spring 2020, implied volatility across US stocks was far above its long-run average, which made each straddle expensive.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's estimated return during each event, using straddles on large US stocks held through earnings announcements. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low, including the premium paid and estimated trading costs.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500, implied volatility and interest rates, which are then applied to the strategy's straddles expected to be held through results in that month.
